headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and unrestricted-code pair: prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading actions are all plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads/writes shared files and uses MCP, while Open Interpreter can access the clipboard, filesystem, and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge even without a documented direct channel. The pathway is not provably blocked, so I rate it medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ECC ingests files from the shared workspace as trusted instructions
IF Open Interpreter copies attacker-controlled content into clipboard or stdout that ECC later parses
mitigations: Disable shared clipboard handoff between the agents
Place each agent in a separate workspace directory
Require manual review of any file both agents touch
Turn off MCP for ECC unless needed
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, hooks, MCP configs, and git history, while Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress. If both run on the same machine, sensitive files or secrets can flow from ECC-managed artifacts into Open Interpreter and then out via model-provider APIs. The default blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share the same local filesystem or home directory
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a remote model provider while reading ECC artifacts
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct OS users
Move ECC state to a dedicated directory not readable by Open Interpreter
Restrict Open Interpreter to a local-only model backend
Rotate any secrets stored in ECC-managed files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. ECC also supports multiple instances with shared state concerns, while Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem. Without locking, concurrent edits to the same repo or config files can corrupt state or overwrite work, matching the high-risk overlap pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or config directory
IF either agent performs git writes without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate git worktrees for each agent
Disable auto-commit or auto-push flows
Add a file lock around shared state paths
requires-engineering: implement transactional merge/lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface emphasizes skills and subagents, while Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code as the invoking user. If ECC outputs instructions, code, or findings that Open Interpreter treats as authoritative, the second agent can turn a mistaken first-step output into real actions. That default action-taking authority makes cascading error high.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes code or shell commands derived from ECC output
IF ECC-produced findings are forwarded without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Insert a verification step between agents
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only mode for the handoff
Use a structured schema for ECC outputs
requires-engineering: add confidence-gated execution policies

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, hooks, and security findings, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data is present on the host, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because ECC state and Open Interpreter’s broad local access are not aligned to a documented compliance boundary. The evidence is insufficient for high, so medium is safer.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the local machine reachable by Open Interpreter
IF ECC session artifacts are retained longer than the organization’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the shared host
Shorten ECC retention settings
Review local file paths before running Open Interpreter
Delete session artifacts after use
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
